newsitem.title: FRANCE: Latvian president suspends death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Latvian president suspends death penalty.

text.p: Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis on Tuesday declared a suspension of the death penalty pending a formal parliamentary vote to abolish it altogether in the Baltic state.

"I can assure you that, awaiting a decision by parliament, I will not refuse any request for pardon", he told the 39-nation Council of Europe. "I thus declare a presidential moratorium on the death sentence."

In a speech to the parliamentary assembly of the Council, which seeks to foster democracy and human rights, Ulmanis said the Latvian parliament would "start discussions on abolition in the immediate future".
Abolishing the death penalty is a condition of membership of the Council, which Latvia joined in 1995, even though founder states like Britain have not ratified abolition.
In June, the parliamentary assembly urged Latvia, Ukraine and Russia to scrap the death penalty or risk sanctions.
A report at the time by Amnesty International said Latvia executed two people by firing squad in January 1996 and two others were on death row.
Ulmanis, re-elected in June, reiterated his country wanted to join the European Union and NATO. "Latvia is prepared to participate in a united Europe," he said.
